name: @sheetsmcp/server

tools.name: google_accounts
tools.description: Manage the Google accounts Sheets MCP can use. list: show signed-in accounts and the default. add: sign in to a Google account (opens a browser sign-in; also use this when a sign-in has expired). remove: sign an account out and revoke access. set_default: choose the account used for new spreadsheets.

email.description: For remove/set_default: the account's email or a unique part of it

tools.name: find_spreadsheet
tools.description: Find a spreadsheet by name among the ones the user has opened or created with Sheets MCP before (the list is kept on their computer). Use it when the user names a sheet instead of pasting a link, e.g. "my budget sheet". It can't search the rest of their Google Drive: if nothing matches, ask for the link. Leave query empty to list the most recent.

query.description: All or part of the spreadsheet's name

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Create a new Google Sheets spreadsheet.

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: get_spreadsheet_info
tools.description: Get a spreadsheet's title, tabs (sizes, frozen rows/cols), charts (ids, types, data ranges), named ranges, and the first few rows of each tab. Call this first to understand a sheet's layout.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: read_range
tools.description: Read cell contents from a range, or its formatting with mode "formats". Large ranges are truncated; use next_range to continue.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

mode.description: values = as displayed; formulas = show formulas instead of results; raw = unformatted numbers; formats = cell formatting (fill, font, alignment, number format, borders) as a style table plus a per-row map of style ids, with merges, banding, conditional formats, column widths, frozen panes and gridlines

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: read_ranges
tools.description: Read several ranges in one call, across any tabs. Faster than calling read_range repeatedly. Each range is truncated to its share of max_cells; use its next_range with read_range to continue.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

items.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

mode.description: values = as displayed; formulas = show formulas instead of results; raw = unformatted numbers

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: write_range
tools.description: Write values and/or formulas starting at the top-left cell of the range. Input is parsed like typing into the UI (formulas, dates, percentages work). Previous contents are saved for undo_last. Returns any formula errors found after writing.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: Top-left cell or full range, e.g. "Sheet1!B2"

values.description: 2D array of rows. Strings starting with = are formulas.

dry_run.description: Only show what would be overwritten

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: fill_range
tools.description: Fill cells from a source block, like dragging the fill handle or pasting onto a bigger selection: the source's formulas (relative references shift), values and formatting repeat across the destination. Use it after writing one row or column of formulas to extend them across a table, instead of sending every column. With continue_series, patterns continue instead (1, 2, 3 → 4, 5, 6; Jan → Feb; dates). The destination's previous contents are saved for undo_last. Returns any formula errors found after filling.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

source.description: The cells to fill from, e.g. "Model!O25:O97"

destination.description: The cells to fill, e.g. "Model!P25:AE97" (it may include the source). For continue_series it must sit right after, or right before, the source in the same rows or columns

paste.description: all = formulas, values and formatting; formulas = formulas and values without formatting; values = results as plain values; formats = formatting only

continue_series.description: Extend the pattern in the source (like the fill handle) instead of repeating it

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: append_rows
tools.description: Append rows after the last row of data in a table (detected from the given range or tab).

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: Tab name or table range, e.g. "Sales" or "Sales!A:F"

values.description: 2D array of rows. Strings starting with = are formulas.

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: clear_range
tools.description: Clear values and formulas in a range (formatting is kept). Previous contents are saved for undo_last.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: find_replace
tools.description: Find and replace text across a tab or the whole spreadsheet. Not undoable - consider read_range first.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

sheet.description: Limit to this tab (default: all tabs)

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: undo_last
tools.description: Undo the most recent write_range, append_rows, or clear_range made through this server (restores values/formulas only, not formatting or structure). History is kept in memory until the server restarts.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: manage_tab
tools.description: Add, delete, rename, or duplicate a tab (sheet).

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

tab.description: Existing tab (for delete/rename/duplicate), or new tab name for add

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: insert_rows_or_columns
tools.description: Insert blank rows or columns before a given row number or column letter.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

before.description: Row number (e.g. "5") or column letter (e.g. "C") to insert before

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: delete_rows_or_columns
tools.description: Delete entire rows (e.g. "Sheet1!5:7") or columns (e.g. "Sheet1!C:D"). Not undoable.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: Whole-row range like "Tab!5:7" or whole-column range like "Tab!C:D"

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: freeze
tools.description: Freeze header rows and/or columns on a tab. Use 0 to unfreeze.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: resize_columns
tools.description: Set column widths in pixels, or auto-fit them to content when width is omitted.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: merge_cells
tools.description: Merge or unmerge cells in a range.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: format_range
tools.description: Apply formatting to a range: font styles, colors, number formats, alignment, wrapping, borders. Only provided options are changed. To style several ranges differently in one go, use format_ranges.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: format_ranges
tools.description: Apply different formatting to several ranges in one call (same options as format_range, one entry per range): headers, input cells, number formats, borders and so on for a whole tab at once. Ranges may repeat; later entries win where they overlap.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

items.description: One entry per range, each with the formatting to apply there

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: add_conditional_format
tools.description: Add a conditional formatting rule: either a condition (e.g. NUMBER_GREATER, TEXT_CONTAINS, CUSTOM_FORMULA) with a style, or a color scale.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

type.description: Google ConditionType: NUMBER_GREATER, NUMBER_LESS, NUMBER_BETWEEN, NUMBER_EQ, TEXT_CONTAINS, TEXT_EQ, BLANK, NOT_BLANK, DATE_BEFORE, CUSTOM_FORMULA, ...

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: sort_range
tools.description: Sort rows within a range by one or more columns.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

has_header.description: Keep the first row of the range in place

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: set_filter
tools.description: Turn on a basic filter (filter buttons in the header row) for a range, or clear the tab's filter.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: Data range including header, or tab name when clearing

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: set_data_validation
tools.description: Add data validation to a range: dropdown list, dropdown from a range, checkbox, number range, custom formula - or clear it.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'My Tab'!B:B", or a tab name

strict.description: Reject invalid input (vs. show a warning)

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: add_chart
tools.description: Create a chart from a data range. The first column is the X axis/labels; each following column is a series. Use a header row for series names.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

anchor_cell.description: Where to place the chart's top-left, e.g. "Sales!F2" (default: right of the data)

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: update_chart
tools.description: Change an existing chart: its title, type, data range, stacking, position or size. Only the options you give are changed. Chart ids come from get_spreadsheet_info or add_chart.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

data_range.description: New data, laid out as for add_chart: first column labels, then one column per series

anchor_cell.description: Move the chart's top-left corner here, e.g. "Sales!F2"

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.description: Delete a chart. Chart ids come from get_spreadsheet_info or add_chart. Not undoable through undo_last.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

tools.name: add_pivot_table
tools.description: Summarize a table with a pivot table: group by one or more columns, and total, count or average others. It goes on a new tab unless anchor_cell is given. The source range needs a header row; refer to columns by header name or letter.

tools.description: Send raw Google Sheets API batchUpdate requests for anything the other tools don't cover (e.g. named ranges, protected ranges, pivot tables, row heights, hiding rows, updating charts). Requests use sheetId numbers from get_spreadsheet_info.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets link or spreadsheet ID. The name of a spreadsheet used with Sheets MCP before also works

account.description: Google account to use: an email or unique part of one (e.g. "acme.com"). Default: the account that can open the spreadsheet, else the default account.

instructions: Sheets MCP lets you read and edit the user's Google Sheets. The first time the user brings up spreadsheets in a conversation, briefly offer what you can do (summarize a sheet, add columns and formulas, clean up formatting, sort and filter, add dropdowns, build charts, create new spreadsheets) and ask which sheet. If the show_recent_sheets tool is available, call it whenever the user wants to work on a spreadsheet without pasting a link or naming one that matches exactly ("let's work on my sheets", "the budget one"), and when a name matches several: they pick from the sheets they've worked on, or paste a link. Don't call it again once they've picked. Without show_recent_sheets, call find_spreadsheet when they name a sheet: it knows the spreadsheets they've used with Sheets MCP before. Neither can search their Google Drive, so ask for the link if nothing matches. When several Google accounts are connected, some tools reply that the account must be confirmed: ask the user which account to use, then call the tool again with `account` set to their choice. Never pick an account for them. If the show_range tool is available, call it FIRST whenever the user asks you to look at or change a spreadsheet, before reading or editing: the user then watches each read and edit happen live. Call it once for each request from the user, and again when a tool result says the live view is out of their sight. If you've already started without it, call it right away; it catches up on what you've done. The live view only draws in the Claude desktop app and claude.ai. When your context indicates the user is on another device (a device hint saying their computer is idle, or a message from a phone or Remote Control), don't call show_range; the tool results then say how to report instead: a short summary in your final reply of the turn (what you did in plain words, the few results that changed as before → after, and one link to the area), since phone apps condense text written between tool calls. Go back to the live view once a message shows they're at the computer again.
